Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: The Farm Suggested vocabulary chicken, sheep, goat, cow, donkey, cat, crop, hay,
Topic 9.1: Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of The Farm Suggested vocabulary chicken, sheep, goat, cow, donkey, cat, crop, hay, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to pronounce words correctly? 2. Why do we need to respond to instructions properly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. pick out words and phrases with the target letter- sound combinations: - cr as in crop - /ɜː/ as in sir, first, thirst - / eɪ / as in say; grey, - /aɪ/ as in fly, cry - words ending with letter y pronounced as /i/ as in baby, - / ə / as in words ending with as far, car.

2. pronounce words and phrases with the target letter- sound combinations.

3. practise pronunciation of words using minimal pairs/rhyming words.

4. listen to and identify the vocabulary related to the theme as used in short sentences/short paragraphs/teacher read aloud stories.

5. articulate vocabulary related to the theme correctly.

6. construct sentences using the new words. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. pick out words and phrases with the target letter- sound combinations: - cr as in crop - /ɜː/ as in sir, first, thirst - / eɪ / as in say; grey, - /aɪ/ as in fly, cry - words ending with letter y pronounced as /i/ as in baby, - / ə / as in words ending with as far, car.
2. pronounce words and phrases with the target letter- sound combinations.
3. practise pronunciation of words using minimal pairs/rhyming words.
4. listen to and identify the vocabulary related to the theme as used in short sentences/short paragraphs/teacher read aloud stories.
5. articulate vocabulary related to the theme correctly.
6. construct sentences using the new words. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration; the learner’s ability to listen keenly and actively is enhanced as they listen to texts and identify vocabulary related

to the theme correctly.

Values:
Love is enhanced as the learner portrays a caring attitude towards animals

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social -economic issues; animal welfare education is enhanced as learners get information on how to take good care of farm animals.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Correct pronunciation is emphasised in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.
